[
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "danger (Old French dangier) = lordship, power; woman (Old English wīfmann) = female human; dangerous woman = one who holds power over men",
    "reading": "A woman with sovereign power, feared because she wields authority traditionally reserved for men.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr", "ang"],
    "source": "OED, s.v. danger, woman",
    "confidence": 0.7
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "dan + ger + ous + wo + man; dan (Hebrew) = judge; ger (French) = to manage; ous (Greek) = being; wo (Chinese) = I/me; man = human",
    "reading": "The judging, self-managing being — the 'I' who is both judge and judged.",
    "languages": ["en", "he", "fr", "grc", "zh"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "dangerous (English) ~ d'angereuse (Old French) = of the anguished one; woman ~ woe + man (English) = sorrow-bringer",
    "reading": "She who brings anguish and sorrow — the woman of the wound, not the weapon.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "Dangerous Woman → 'A wound grows in me' (letters rearranged: A WOUND GROWS IN ME)",
    "reading": "The danger is internal — a growing wound that transforms the woman into a source of peril.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "D.W. → D = Delta (change, gate), W = double-u (double V = victory, or womb); D.W. = Delta of the Womb",
    "reading": "The gate of transformation through the womb — a dangerous passage into new life or death.",
    "languages": ["en", "grc", "la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "D = door (daleth, Hebrew); W = water (double u, waves); D + W = door over water; woman = vessel (vase, Latin vas)",
    "reading": "A vessel that opens a door across the waters — dangerous to cross, yet the only crossing.",
    "languages": ["en", "he", "la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "D=4, A=1, N=14, G=7, E=5, R=18, O=15, U=21, S=19, W=23, O=15, M=13, A=1, N=14 → sum = 170; 1+7+0=8; 8 = infinity, regeneration",
    "reading": "The dangerous woman is the infinite cycle — she destroys and renews, her number is the eternal spiral.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "woman (Old English wīfmann) = wīf (woman) + mann (person); dangerous (Latin dominarium, via Old French) = belonging to a lord; thus 'lordly female person'",
    "reading": "A female person who is lordly — not a lady under a lord, but a lord herself.",
    "languages": ["en", "la", "fr"],
    "source": "OED, s.v. woman; Lewis & Short, dominarium",
    "confidence": 0.6
  }
]
